messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: stan c++ library
parts:
It is not fully documented or super-stable. But if you clone the source from github and open

$STAN_HOME/doc/api/html/index.html


in a web browser, you can see the doxygen version of the documentation.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: stan c++ library [prob fun, grad, samplers]
parts:
I'm afraid there aren't any simple examples we can point you to.

The best thing to do is run stanc and look at the generated
model code. It exposes functions that expose the log density
and gradient on the unconstrained scale (with and without Jacobian).

As to HMC and NUTS, you'll have to then trace through the
compiled command code. That used to be in stan/gm/command.hpp,
but it's moving to its own repo in CmdStan.

- Bob
